newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan govt mulling freer municipal bond issuance.
newsitem.headline: Japan govt mulling freer municipal bond issuance.

text.p: The Japanese government is mulling a liberalisation of the municipal bond issuing system that would permit municipalities to issue bonds without receiving prior authorisation from the central government, a ministry official said on Tuesday.

"Fundamentally, we want to give local governments more rights to decide their own fund-raising and financial situations, as part of giving them more independence overall," the official at the Home Affairs Ministry's municipal bond division said.

Currently, prefectures and designated cities are required to obtain permission from the Home Affairs Ministry before issuing bonds, while other municipalities must get permission from their local government.

Under the new system, the prefectural governments and designated cities would consult with the Home Affairs Ministry about prospective bond issues. Should agreement not be reached, however, the municipalities could still issue bonds if their local prefectural parliament approved, the official said.
Other municipalities would consult with their local governments prior to any prospective bond issues, he added.

"Although there are still some aspects of municipal funding that the central government must retain final responsibility over, the new system would raise the possibility of a local government being able to issue bonds even if the central government did not approve, as long as nothing about the proposed issue was against the law," the official said.

These points are being pulled together by a committee to promote government decentralisation under the auspices of the Management and Coordination Agency, and will be submitted to the central government in July as one part of a broader recommendation on changes in the relationship between the municipal and central government, he added.
The outstanding balance of municipal bonds is expected to stand at around 108 trillion yen by the end of fiscal 1997/98.
"The new issue system for the munis (municipal bonds) means a more smooth, frequent supply of bonds," said a senior trader at a city bank's securities arm.
Currently, issuance of municipal bonds tends to be heavily concentrated in March through May, which negatively affects the demand-supply balance of the overall yen debt market.

Traders said that even if the new system is adopted, the issue volume of municipal bonds is unlikely to expand given the current government effort in balancing the state as well as municipal government budget.
